headline: Law updates the federal charter of the Foundation of the Federal Bar Association, moving many rules from the charter into the group's own bylaws.
what_it_does: The law changes the congressional charter for the Foundation of the Federal Bar Association. It drops the requirement that the foundation be based in Washington, D.C., and lets its board choose its main office location. Membership terms, board duties, and officer elections will now be set in the bylaws instead of the charter. It also changes rules on pay, grants, loans, political activity, and what happens to the foundation's assets if it closes.

who_it_affects.group: Foundation of the Federal Bar Association
who_it_affects.how: The foundation gains more control over its own rules through its bylaws and is no longer required to be based in Washington, D.C.
They may receive reasonable pay or expense reimbursement, cannot take part in political activities in their official roles, and members are now barred from receiving loans from the foundation.
The foundation may pay them reasonable compensation, but they are now barred from receiving loans from it.
A chapter connected to a foundation officer, director, or member may receive grants from the foundation.
If the foundation closes, its remaining assets will be distributed as the board decides instead of going to the Treasury.

when_it_takes_effect: Enacted December 12, 2025; the summary does not state a separate effective date.
